concerns.text: Task T024 implements 'global label permutation' (shuffling across the entire dataset), which directly contradicts the Plan's 'CRITICAL UPDATE' for FR-004 requiring 'stratified permutation within LD blocks'. This semantic weakening violates the statistical validity mandated by the plan to prevent Type I error inflation.

Task T027b introduces a 'baseline correction calculation' using a derived adjustment factor for the KS test. Spec FR-005 explicitly mandates the KS test be run on the 'FULL unfiltered distribution' of scores (inside vs outside/control) without mentioning a derived adjustment factor. This adds a statistical step not present in the spec, violating the constraint that tasks must not silently relax or alter the defined methodology.

Tasks T010b, T011, and T025 contain '[UNRESOLVED-CLAIM]' markers with 'status=not_enough_info'. These tasks are required to satisfy FR-001 (data ingestion), FR-002 (PWM loading), and FR-007 (p-value output). Leaving these critical deliverables in an unresolved state constitutes a failure to preserve the requirement that the system MUST perform these actions.

Task T025a relies on T013b (GC-matched control set) as the primary 'outside' distribution for the KS test. Spec FR-005 defines the comparison as 'SNPs inside GWAS loci against SNPs outside GWAS loci (or the matched control set)'. The task's rigid reliance on the control set without explicitly mapping it to the 'outside GWAS' definition or allowing the genomic background option creates a potential drift from the spec's flexible acceptance criteria.
